item.title: Israeli strike killed two staff outside Gaza clinic, MSF says
item.description:
GENEVA, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontièreshas voiced outrage after an Israeli strike killed two of its staff outside a medical clinic in Gaza late on Friday.

"Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military," it said. "We call for accountability."

Israel's military confirmed the strike but said the two MSF staff were "terrorists posing as humanitarian workers".

item.title: Iran's flogging of singer was warning from anxious hardliners, insiders say
item.description:
By Parisa Hafezi, Emily Giles and Melory Ghazi

DUBAI, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Iran's flogging of a female singer this week for offending public decency was a display of force by an embattled clerical elite straining to uphold public obedience it once took for granted, Iranian insiders say.

Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and four members of her production team received 74 lashes each on Monday for a livestreamed performance in a caravanserai near the holy Shi'ite Muslim city of Qom in which she had bare shoulders, no headscarf and male musicians, defying Iran's theocratic legal code.

item.title: US military repelled drones at UK airbase this month, FT reports
item.description:
Nov 28 (Reuters) - The US military repelled a half dozen drones swarming Britain's RAF Lakenheath base earlier this month, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, saying Iran was suspected of being linked to the incident.

The newspaper, citing people familiar with the matter, said the US deployed counter-drone technology to repel the unmanned aerial systems but that the drones were not retrieved by British or American personnel.

item.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
UN rapporteur to leave for Mexico after halted at Costa Rica airport
item.description:
The UN special rapporteur on Palestinian rights will leave Costa Rica for Mexico on Saturday, after the Costa Rican government denied her entry.

Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide in Gaza and the occupied territories, said Friday that Costa Rica will be held accountable for false "terrorism" accusations it leveled to justify her rejection.

Albanese spoke from the airport serving the capital city San Jose, after being refused entry following her arrival Thursday.

item.title: US military fires on ship violating Iran blockade
US disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
item.description: DUBAI, Nov 27 (Reuters) - The US military said on Friday it disabled a commercial ship that attempted to run the US blockade of Iran, while an adviser to Iran's supreme leader said Tehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut and vowed to break the US embargo.

item.title: Costa Rica bars UN rapporteur on Palestinian territories, drawing concern from rights chief
item.description:
By Paolo Laudani and Alvaro Murillo

Nov 27 (Reuters) - Costa Rica denied entry to the United Nations special rapporteur on the Israeli-occupied Palestinian territories, drawing criticism from UN human rights chief Volker Turk on Friday.

Costa Rica's move put the small Central American country's increasingly close alignment with Washington and Israel on security and foreign policy into the spotlight.

item.title: How foreign navies could reshape Iran’s grip on Hormuz after the war
item.description: A proposed expansion of South Korea's naval mission near the Strait of Hormuz has Tehran unsettled over prospects of a wider war and a potential loss of its leverage in the strategic waterway.

item.title: Tunisia NGO slams 'inhumane' prison conditions after dozens of detainee deaths
item.description:
Tunisia's main rights group on Friday denounced "inhumane" conditions in Tunisian prisons, saying 30 inmates have died since the beginning of summer, the country's hottest on record.

Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths after a summer marked by multiple heatwaves, water shortages and power cuts.

"The situation in prisons is inhumane and catastrophic," said Bassem Trifi, head of the Tunisian League for Human Rights, adding that "overcrowding and the lack of healthcare" in prisons were a major issue.

item.title: UN refugee agency seeks $7.1 bn in 2027
item.description:
The United Nations' refugee agency said on Friday it was seeking a much-reduced $7.1 billion to protect stateless people and respond to emergencies in 2027.

UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned last month that his agency was being "asked to do the impossible", over-stretched by a huge funding shortfall and near record-high population displacements around the world.

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

item.description: OPEC+ is conducting its first-ever review of members' production capacity to guide 2027 output targets and prevent the kind of quota disputes that have driven some countries to leave the cartel.

item.title: War, fear drive Sudanese writer Baraka Sakin's fiction
item.description:
A lifetime of war and persecution has shaped the writing of Sudanese novelist Abdelaziz Baraka Sakin, who has turned the fear and longing that are so central to his experience into his main drive.

The 63-year-old fled Sudan for Europe in 2012 and then returned, dreaming of an end to his forced exile.

But the war that erupted in 2023 and killed more than 200,000 people pushed him out again.

Still, he keeps writing.

item.title: UN urges Costa Rica to let in Palestinians rapporteur
item.description:
The United Nations on Friday urged Costa Rica to urgently reconsider its ban on admitting the UN special rapporteur on Palestinian rights and let her into the country.

Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

Italian lawyer Albanese is the UN special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967.
